name: Hungarian Gulyás
description: Real Hungarian gulyás is genuinely a soup, not a thick stew - it's naturally thickened by the collagen breaking down over a long simmer, not flour, and real technique 'blooms' the paprika briefly off the heat before adding liquid, since burnt paprika turns bitter. Real Hungarians are genuinely generous with paprika - one source's advice is to at least double or triple whatever amount seems reasonable - and real caraway is a defining, non-optional seasoning.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in a little oil, 8-9 minutes, until softened.
Remove the pot briefly from the heat and stir in the paprika and caraway - real technique blooms the paprika off the direct heat for a few seconds, since it burns and turns bitter very easily.
Add the beef and garlic, and brown, 6-7 minutes.
Add the broth and simmer 1-1.5 hours until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the carrot, potato, and bell pepper, and simmer 20-25 minutes more, until everything is tender and the broth has thickened naturally from the collagen.

name: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
description: Paprikás csirke, chicken in a rich paprika-sour cream sauce, is one of Hungary's most beloved dishes, real technique stirring the sour cream in at the very end, off the heat, at room temperature, so it doesn't curdle or turn lumpy.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion, 4-5 minutes, until softened.
Remove from the heat briefly and stir in the paprika, being generous, so it blooms without burning.
Add the chicken and tomatoes, and simmer 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Remove from the heat and stir in the room-temperature sour cream - real technique never lets this boil, since cold sour cream added to a hot pot is what causes curdling.

name: Hungarian Nokedli
description: Nokedli, short, stubby egg dumplings, are the real traditional accompaniment to both gulyás and paprikash, real technique scraping small pieces of batter directly into boiling water.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, egg, salt, and a splash of water into a thick, sticky batter.
Scrape small pieces of the batter directly off a cutting board into a pot of boiling salted water.
Cook 3-4 minutes until they float, then drain.

name: Hungarian Töltött Paprika (Stuffed Peppers)
description: Töltött paprika, peppers stuffed with rice and meat in a paprika-tomato sauce, is a genuine Hungarian comfort staple.
steps_detailed: Par-cook the rice about 10 minutes.
Mix the beef, par-cooked rice, and half the paprika.
Stuff into the peppers, stand in a baking dish, and pour the tomatoes (mixed with the remaining paprika) around and over.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 35-40 minutes until the peppers are tender.

name: Hungarian Mushroom Soup
description: Hungarian mushroom soup, real technique blooms the paprika the same way as gulyás, finished with real sour cream and fresh dill.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and mushrooms, 6-7 minutes.
Remove from heat briefly and stir in the paprika to bloom it without burning.
Add the broth and simmer 15-18 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the sour cream and dill.

name: Hungarian Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad with real sour cream, a common Hungarian side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Toss with the sour cream and vinegar, and dust with paprika.

name: Hungarian Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Hungary.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Hungarian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Hungarian home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Hungarian Paprika Sour Cream Sauce
description: A simple paprika and sour cream sauce, echoing the flavor of paprikash, used across many Hungarian dishes.
steps_detailed: Whisk the paprika into the sour cream and chill before serving.
